questions.q: What does Burkeman conclude about mastering your time?
a: It is impossible, and you should stop trying
It is the key to a successful career
It requires strict daily schedules
It gets easy with the right system
questions.why: The overview says the book argues against the hustler mindset and explains why time cannot be mastered.

questions.q: Why did medieval people place less value on their days on earth?
a: Religion taught them to focus on an afterlife
Their lives were too short to plan ahead
They had no way of measuring time
They worked only during harvest season
questions.why: The first lesson says belief in the afterlife meant people did not count their limited days so carefully.

questions.q: What does the summary say about procrastination?
a: Everyone does it, and a little of it restores energy
Only lazy people give in to it
It should be eliminated from every schedule
It always signals that burnout is coming
questions.why: The second lesson says we are wired to procrastinate and that rest between tasks leaves us fresher.

questions.q: How does Burkeman suggest you get more tasks finished?
a: Rank them by importance and work through them in order
Start with the quickest ones to build momentum
Work on several at once to save time
Delegate anything that feels repetitive
questions.why: The second lesson says proper prioritizing, one task at a time, is more effective than multitasking.

questions.q: What does the author recommend doing with the spare time you gain?
a: Spend it on hobbies and people you love
Take on new projects to stay sharp
Turn every hobby into extra income
Schedule it for maximum efficiency
questions.why: The third lesson says leisure, family and being mediocre at a hobby boost productivity in the long run.
